defects.root_cause: Two clocks: collection UTC, preflight local.
defects.regression_test: validation/scripts/test_utc_clock.py (asserts _utc_today() reads the UTC calendar day, not local)

Added a dedicated behavioral test (test_utc_clock.py) that makes UTC and local dates diverge; verified it goes RED under the mutation. This is the mutation harness catching a real test blind spot.

defects.description: The submitted SDR's dailyData series, 30-day/1-year window summaries, and per-metric daily series used the host's LOCAL date.today() as the window ceiling, while the collectors stamp every datapoint in UTC (datetime.now(timezone.utc)). On a host west of UTC near midnight, a genuine current-day UTC observation is dated after the lagging local 'today' and is silently dropped from the submitted document -- a silent under-report of measured coverage that is invisible in UTC CI. Same two-clock class as F10, which only fixed sdr.py:_utc_today() (preflight) and never touched the SDR builder.
defects.root_cause: Two clocks: collection UTC, SDR-builder window ceiling local. Found in the whole-repo adversarial audit (not among the recent-change set F01-F10; build_sdr.py had no dedicated clock coverage).

defects.description: There was no single definition of release-ready. GitHub required only the `validate` status check on main, so a red audit-gate or security-scan did not block a merge; the AWS RELEASE_MODE build ran the mutation runner and oracle but not Bandit; `sdr.py release` ran neither. v1.4.0 (commit c7d43bd) was published while its audit-gate was red (MUT-F10 survived, 9 killed / 1 survived) and its release notes claimed 10 killed / 0 survived; the tag was unsigned although docs/versioning.md requires a signed tag, and no assets (manifest, attestation, SBOM) were attached.
defects.root_cause: Three executors each owned their own step list; the only enforced one was the weakest.
defects.fix_commit: this PR -- audit/release_gate.py holds the one step list (audit: oracle, runner self-test, runner, tree-clean; security: Bandit); CI jobs, RELEASE_MODE, and cmd_release all execute it; a `release-gate` aggregate job (needs all three, if: always()) is the single required status check on main; release.yml refuses unsigned or mismatched tags, re-runs the whole gate on the tagged commit, and attaches manifest + attestation + SBOM + bundle; cmd_release now instructs `git tag -s`. v1.4.0 is superseded, not moved.
defects.regression_test: automation/pipeline/test_release_gate.py (AUD-F12 block: definition completeness, CI aggregate wiring, RELEASE_MODE parity, cmd_release parity, signed-tag release workflow)
defects.mutation: MUT-F12: drop the mutation-runner step from release_gate.SECTIONS['audit']; expect RED

defects.description: A mutation whose target text was absent was reported SKIP, and skips did not fail the gate. A harmless refactor of a guarded line therefore silently disarmed the protection for a closed defect while the ledger still said mutation_verified: the gate failed open on refactoring.
defects.root_cause: SKIP was designed for a defect fixed on an unmerged branch and treated as benign; it is indistinguishable from a disarmed mutation.
defects.fix_commit: this PR -- any skipped mutation fails the gate; the two honest resolutions are retargeting the mutation or running on the branch that carries the fix
defects.regression_test: audit/test_mutation_runner.py::F13 (a mutation with an absent target makes run() exit non-zero)
defects.mutation: MUT-F13: `if skipped:` -> `if False:` in run(); expect RED

defects.description: Nothing checked that a CLOSED + mutation_verified ledger entry corresponded to an executed, killed runner mutation, so the ledger could claim a mutation the runner did not contain (this happened once before: a MUT-F02 was ledgered before it existed), and a runner mutation could exist with no ledger entry.
defects.root_cause: Ledger and runner were two hand-maintained lists with no reconciliation.
defects.fix_commit: this PR -- run() reconciles: every CLOSED + mutation_verified defect maps to exactly one runner entry whose outcome this run was 'killed', and every runner entry maps to such a defect; any disagreement fails the gate
defects.regression_test: audit/test_mutation_runner.py::F14 (missing runner entry, unledgered mutation, survived/skipped outcome, duplicate ids, and the real ledger vs real runner structural agreement)
defects.mutation: MUT-F14: reconcile_ledger returns [] before checking; expect RED

defects.description: Most AWS list/describe calls read ONE page (KMS list_keys, CloudFormation list_stacks, Config conformance packs and rule compliance, WAF web ACLs, EC2 security groups, ECR repositories, IAM users/roles/access keys, CodePipeline pipelines, DynamoDB tables, Backup resources, Access Analyzer findings), and several of them produced measured/total ratios from page 1 alone, so a favorable first page could become a boundary-wide passing metric. defects.mutation: MUT-F15: _paginate returns after the first page regardless of token; expect RED

defects.description: Per-resource loops did `except: continue`, so an unreadable resource vanished from the denominator: 50 in scope, 10 readable, all 10 pass read as 10/10 = 100 percent. S3 encryption tracked `unmeasured` in text only, so 1 encrypted readable bucket + 99 AccessDenied buckets still scored 1/1. collect_s3 public-access counted ANY exception as evaluated-not-blocked, turning a denied read into adverse telemetry.
defects.root_cause: Facts carried only measured/total (evaluated) with no scope or unknown count, and no coverage policy separate from the pass ratio.
defects.fix_commit: this PR -- facts carry scope_total / evaluated_total / unknown_total; a fact whose evaluated coverage is below MIN_EVALUATED_COVERAGE (0.95, project policy; offering may tighten via telemetry_min_coverage) is withheld from scoring (never scored as a failure) and named in the datapoint's coverage_gaps; the datapoint carries aggregate coverage; only a response that establishes absence (NoSuchPublicAccessBlockConfiguration, NoSuchLifecycleConfiguration) is evaluated
defects.regression_test: automation/metrics/test_append_metrics.py::test_f17_low_evaluated_coverage_is_not_a_confident_pass, ::test_f17_one_readable_bucket_of_100_does_not_score, ::test_f17_full_coverage_scores_and_carries_coverage, ::test_f17_no_scope_info_still_scores_legacy_facts; automation/collectors/test_collectors.py::test_f17_kms_unreadable_key_is_unknown_not_dropped_from_scope, ::test_f17_s3_public_access_denied_is_unknown_not_a_failure, ::test_f17_all_reads_denied_is_unknown_not_a_pass
defects.mutation: MUT-F17: _posture_score ignores evaluated coverage (if False); expect RED

defects.requirement: FRC-CSX-MOT persistent validation (durable history lost updates)
defects.description: The scheduled build did GET metric-history.json -> modify locally -> PUT the same key with no compare-and-swap. Two overlapping runs could both read version N and whichever uploaded last silently discarded the other's datapoints; S3 versioning kept the bytes recoverable but nothing noticed.

defects.fix_commit: this PR -- publish_history.py restores with the object's ETag and publishes with If-Match (If-None-Match:* on first run); a 412 returns exit 3 and the buildspec re-runs restore -> append -> publish (bounded); every run's observations are archived append-only under metrics/observations/<date>/<run>.json with If-None-Match:* (an existing record for the same run id is kept, never overwritten)

defects.description: The 45-day maximum-gap continuity check was hard-coded and presented in blocker text as if it were the FedRAMP requirement; FedRAMP states no cadence and no maximum gap. The nearby comment claimed an adaptive tolerance of max(4x median, 45 days) that the code never applied, so the documented behavior and the enforced behavior disagreed.

defects.regression_test: validation/scripts/test_mot_continuity.py (F21 block: default, override, numeric string, above-ceiling invalid, zero invalid, non-integer invalid, tolerance drives the verdict, preflight wiring and wording)

defects.requirement: Supply-chain reproducibility of the framework's own build (SBOM closure; KSI-SCR by analogy)
defects.component: requirements.lock (new); Makefile lock target; every CI workflow and buildspec install step; validation/scripts/build_sbom.py (consumer); validation/scripts/test_lock_closure.py (new)
defects.description: Top-level Python dependencies were pinned and Actions were SHA-pinned, but there was no committed hash-locked transitive closure: CI installed with plain `pip -r requirements-ci.txt`, so transitive packages resolved to whatever the index served on the day, and the SBOM honestly admitted it enumerated only the direct pins.
defects.root_cause: The lock-aware SBOM mechanism existed (`make lock`) but no lock had ever been produced by a resolver; generating one from an installed environment would have been wrong (dev/test packages, drifted versions), so it was deferred.
defects.fix_commit: this PR -- requirements.lock resolved by uv (a real resolver run against the index, not the installed environment) for the linux/py3.12 CI target from requirements.txt + requirements-ci.txt with --generate-hashes: 27 packages, every one hashed; every workflow and buildspec installs with `pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.lock`; the Makefile lock target uses the same uv invocation; the SBOM is now the resolved closure with hashes (27 components, scope resolved-closure-with-hashes), fingerprinted by the release manifest
defects.regression_test: validation/scripts/test_lock_closure.py (lock present and hashed; every direct pin at the same version in the lock; SBOM rebuilt in-process equals the committed SBOM and covers every lock package with hashes; every installer uses --require-hashes -r requirements.lock)
defects.mutation: MUT-F25: build_sbom ignores the committed lock (lock = None); expect RED

defects.requirement: Evidence integrity: a verified digest must attest the assertion the reader sees (AU-9, AU-10; KSI-MLA / SDR evidence non-repudiation)
defects.component: automation/collectors/evidence_wiring.py (fact_to_evidence, canonical_payload, BOUND_FIELDS); validation/scripts/validate_evidence.py (_resolve_source, classify_entry); automation/collectors/evidence_lifecycle.py (verify_integrity); automation/collectors/sign_evidence.py (docs)
defects.description: The content hash (and therefore the KMS signature over it) covered only the sanitized xSourceFact. evidenceDescription, evidenceText, evidenceLocation and lastUpdated were outside the digest, so an entry whose description had been rewritten from a resource-specific observation to 'All customer resources fully compliant' still classified `verified`. Reproduced with the public helpers at 2f72a15 (external end-to-end audit 2026-09-26, F1).
defects.root_cause: The digest was designed as a source-fact traceability aid and the displayed fields were added around it later; nothing bound the interpretation to the attestation.
defects.fix_commit: this PR -- the digest is computed LAST over evidence_wiring.canonical_payload(entry) (evidenceType, evidenceDescription, evidenceLocation, evidenceText, lastUpdated, xSourceFact); the verifier recomputes over the same projection of the entry itself, so a change to any displayed field is a HARD INTEGRITY FAILED; the legacy inline `source_fact` shape (digest over the raw fact only) can only reach a FINDING, and is HARD under a signing-required signer or with a signature present; the fail-closed missing-hash-implementation check now runs before source resolution; evidence_lifecycle.verify_integrity checks both the fact projection and the bound digest
defects.regression_test: validation/scripts/test_evidence_integrity.py (test_f26_each_displayed_field_tamper_is_hard: each of evidenceDescription/evidenceText/evidenceLocation/lastUpdated/evidenceType tampered independently -> hard; test_f26_legacy_unbound_shape_cannot_be_verified; test_f26_signature_binds_displayed_fields); the suite's fixtures now use the production fact_to_evidence shape
defects.mutation: MUT-F26: digest computed over xSourceFact only (canonical_payload(evidence) -> evidence['xSourceFact']); expect RED

defects.requirement: Evidence completeness across a multi-account boundary: every account/region/check observation must have a distinct, verifiable identity and the raw account must never enter the package (CDS-CSO sensitivity; KSI-PIY inventory completeness)
defects.component: automation/collectors/evidence_wiring.py (scope_id, new_run_id, _pointer, _sanitize_fact_for_evidence, fact_to_evidence, observation_identity, attach_evidence); automation/collectors/collect_multi_account.py (run_id/scope stamping, scope_map, write_private_store, --out)
defects.description: Multi-account collection tagged facts with `account`, but evidence conversion dropped it from xSourceFact and built the pointer from service/check/region only; attach_evidence de-duplicated by that pointer. Two facts for different accounts with the same service/check/region, one PASS and one FAIL, produced ONE entry (the PASS) and the FAIL was silently discarded; with replace=True both remained but shared one pointer. Reproduced at 2f72a15 (external audit F2). An assessor could not reconstruct account-level coverage from the sanitized evidence.
defects.root_cause: The sanitizer correctly refused to export the account id (sensitive) but offered no non-sensitive substitute, so scope identity was lost rather than protected; the multi-account CLI only printed a summary and never exercised the export path.
defects.fix_commit: this PR -- an account-tagged fact carries an OPAQUE scope id (HMAC-SHA256 under a deployment-private key SDR_EVIDENCE_SCOPE_KEY, or a caller-supplied slug-safe alias that may not be the account itself) in the signed payload AND the evidence object key, plus the collector run id; a fact tagged with an account that has no way to derive a scope is REFUSED (EvidenceExportError), never silently dropped or exported; attach_evidence de-duplicates on (location, scope, observation) so two scopes' opposite findings and two runs of one scope all survive; collect_multi_account stamps run_id/scope on every fact, exposes scope_map() and writes facts + the PRIVATE scope->account map to the git-excluded store via --out
defects.regression_test: automation/collectors/test_evidence_wiring.py (test_f27_two_accounts_opposite_findings_both_kept, test_f27_account_never_enters_the_entry, test_f27_scope_is_keyed_and_deterministic, test_f27_account_tagged_fact_without_scope_is_refused_not_dropped, test_f27_run_id_scopes_the_pointer_and_dedup_identity, test_f27_no_account_no_scope_stays_backward_compatible); automation/collectors/test_multi_account.py (test_f27_two_accounts_opposite_findings_survive_end_to_end through the real collect_across_accounts -> attach_evidence path; unkeyed run refused at export; private store carries the scope map)
defects.mutation: MUT-F27: scope dropped from the evidence pointer (_pointer ignores scope); expect RED

defects.requirement: Non-sensitive public package: no environment-identifying detail (hostnames, IPs, ARNs, identifiers) in customer-facing evidence (CDS-CSO-*; FedRAMP sensitivity guidance)
defects.description: Free-form collector `detail` was copied verbatim into evidenceDescription and (first 120 chars) into xSourceFact.summary, while the generated-artifact sensitive-pattern gate detected only a 12-digit account id, an AKIA access key and a private-key header. A synthetic detail carrying an internal hostname and 10.23.45.67 reached both fields and the gate did not fire. First-party collectors emit bounded counts, but third-party adapters and callers can pass arbitrary text. Reproduced at 2f72a15 (external audit F3).
defects.root_cause: The projection allow-listed FIELDS but not the CONTENT of the free-text field it kept; the output gate was tuned to credentials, not environment identifiers.
defects.fix_commit: this PR -- every free-text field (detail, status) is scrubbed (ARN, access key, key material, email, URL, IPv6, IPv4, account id, hostname/FQDN, long opaque token) and length-bounded before it enters an entry; every identifier that becomes an object-key segment (service, check, region, scope, run_id) must be slug-safe or the fact is refused; the bundle gate additionally flags IPv4, IPv6, ARNs and internal hostnames as an independent backstop; first-party detail strings are unchanged by the scrub (regression proves it)
defects.regression_test: automation/collectors/test_evidence_wiring.py (test_f28_hostname_and_ip_in_detail_are_scrubbed, test_f28_arn_account_key_email_url_token_are_scrubbed, test_f28_first_party_details_are_untouched, test_f28_detail_and_status_are_bounded, test_f28_key_segments_must_be_slug_safe, test_f28_csv_adapter_check_from_raw_is_slug_checked); automation/sdrscan/test_checks.py (test_f28_bundle_gate_catches_ip_arn_and_internal_host)
defects.mutation: MUT-F28: summary copied verbatim without scrubbing (scrub_text(detail, SUMMARY_MAX) -> detail[:SUMMARY_MAX]); expect RED
